items.now: If SOL moves $1, this position gains or loses about $21.82. Delta is positive, so you benefit if SOL rises.
items.shift: As SOL falls toward your $64 short put, delta grows, so each further $1 drop hurts more. As SOL rises, delta shrinks toward zero and the position goes quiet.

items.now: Each day that passes with SOL roughly unchanged, this position gains about $3.55.
items.shift: Theta grows as expiry approaches, especially near the short strike, so the last two weeks earn fastest but are also the jumpiest. If SOL falls below your $58 long put, theta can turn against you.

items.now: How fast delta changes: a $1 move in SOL changes delta by about 1.413 (a $5 move shifts your $-per-$1 figure by about $7.06). Gamma is negative, so moves feed on themselves against you.
items.shift: Gamma spikes when SOL is near $64 close to expiry. That is when small moves cause big swings in profit and loss, and the usual moment to close or roll.

items.now: If implied volatility rises 1 point, this position loses about $4.58; if it falls 1 point, it gains about $4.58. You are short vega: you want fear to fade.
items.shift: A selloff usually lifts IV, so you can show a paper loss before SOL reaches your strikes. Vega shrinks as expiry approaches, so later in the trade price matters more than IV.

steps.title: Take profit
steps.level: Spread costs $0.58 or less to buy back
steps.why: Most of the reward arrives early, while the last weeks carry most of the risk. A resting order takes the profit for you, so there is no decision to freeze on.
steps.ticket: BUY 20 contracts (200 SOL) of the spread: buy SOL_USDC-25DEC26-64-P, sell SOL_USDC-25DEC26-58-P. Limit $0.58 per SOL (net debit). Good till cancelled.

steps.title: Price stop (main protection)
steps.result: Loss about $348 instead of the $968 maximum
steps.why: Set where the trade has lost 1.5x the credit, allowing for implied vol rising 1 point per 1% drop and 3 days passing. Without the vol allowance it would sit at $61.34: the jump in fear moves the exit earlier.
steps.ticket: BUY 20 contracts (200 SOL) of SOL_USDC-25DEC26-64-P only. Trigger: SOL index price at or below $61.79. Limit $9.55. Reduce-only. Good till cancelled.

steps.title: Backup stop (gaps and fear spikes)
steps.level: Short put's mark price at or above $7.35
steps.result: Fires if the put you sold gets that expensive by any route: a gap down, a fear spike, or both
steps.why: A second trigger on the option itself, in case SOL jumps past the price stop or implied vol spikes first. Whichever fires first closes the trade; reduce-only stops the other doing anything.
steps.ticket: BUY 20 contracts (200 SOL) of SOL_USDC-25DEC26-64-P only. Trigger: mark price at or above $7.35. Limit $9.55. Reduce-only. Good till cancelled.

steps.title: Time exit
steps.result: Close whatever is still open, win or lose
steps.why: In the last week gamma is at its highest: small moves cause big swings. This one cannot be a resting order, so the scanner will flag it.
steps.ticket: On 2026-12-18: cancel the other orders, then buy back the spread at the market's offer.

exit_plan.after_stop: Only the short put is closed. Your long put stays: it can only gain value if SOL keeps falling, so hold it as a free hedge or sell it later. A stop firing means SOL is cheaper: that is a planned moment for your USDC reserve to buy spot.
exit_plan.order_note: On Deribit a buy that triggers when SOL falls may be listed as a 'take' order type rather than 'stop'. Check the trigger direction on the test site before using it with real money.
